newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks leap to new high in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks leap to new high in active trade.

text.p: The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange (ZSE) leapt to a new record level on Tuesday as rains continued to underpin a bullrun which began two months ago.
The 57-share industrial index soared 179.55 points -- or two percent -- to smash through the key 9,000 psychological barrier, ending the day at a new all time peak of 9,130.68.

"It's a question of sentiment. It's raining and the economy is forecast to grow by at least seven percent this year," one broker said, adding: "Interest rates (on the money market) have been coming down so people feel the stock exchange is the place for their money."
The brokers, however, said the market was likely to correct next week. "Anything that goes up will come down so there's bound to be a correction at some point," one said.

Leading Tuesday's winners on the ZSE, bankers Barclays and clothing retailer Edgars soared 200 cents each to 2,800 and 4,200 respectively, blue-chip conglomerate Delta at 3,900 and clothing retailer Truworths at 1,200 both leapt 100 cents.

Clothing and furniture retailer Tedco jumped 70 cents to 1,120, finance house Finhold rose 25 cents to 750, tobacco group TSL gained 20 cents to 740, glass firm PGI added 10 cents to 560 as did hotel chain Zimsun to 420.

A handful of counters bucked the trend, notably horticultural company Ariston which dropped 100 cents to 2,400, transport group Clan which shed 20 cents to 460 and publishing group Zimpapers which lost 10 cents to 2,690.
In minings, Falgold traded 15 cents down at 90 but Wankie Colliery put on five cents to 635 in reasonable turnover.
The seven-share mining index edged 1.63 points up to 1,124.17.
